items.title: 4.2 Solution of First-Order and First-Degree Differential Equations (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 129 (PDF 131): 4.2 general form dy/dx = f(x,y), differential form M dx + N dy = 0, Examples (i)-(ii), solution, initial value condition, IVP; text before 4.2.1

blocks.text: Pichhle hisse (4.1) mein humne seekha tha ke differential equation kya hoti hai, aur us ka order aur degree kaise dekhte hain. Ab asal kaam shuru hota hai: in equations ko solve karna, yani woh function dhoondna jo equation ko poora kare. Is section mein hum sirf un equations ki baat karenge jo first order aur first degree hain, kyunke yahi sab se aasaan aur sab se zyada kaam aane wali hain.
Kitab sab se pehle first order aur first degree differential equation ki general form (aam shakal) batati hai:

blocks.text_alt: d y by d x equals f of x and y

blocks.text: Yahan \(f\) do variables \(x\) aur \(y\) ka function hai, jo \(xy\)-plane ke kisi region (hisse) par defined hai. Matlab right side par kuch bhi ho sakta hai jis mein \(x\) aur \(y\) hon. Is equation ko hamesha differential form mein bhi likha ja sakta hai:

blocks.text_alt: M of x and y times d x plus N of x and y times d y equals zero

blocks.text: Yahan \(M(x, y)\) aur \(N(x, y)\) bhi \(x\) aur \(y\) ke functions hain: \(M\) woh hai jo \(dx\) ke saath laga hai aur \(N\) woh jo \(dy\) ke saath laga hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Zara yaad karein ke "first order" aur "first degree" ka matlab kya tha. First order ka matlab: equation mein sab se oonchi derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hai, \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) jaisi koi cheez nahi. First degree ka matlab: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ki power sirf 1 hai, us ka square ya cube nahi. Isi liye aisi har equation ko \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ke liye solve kar ke \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) likh sakte hain.
Do shaklein kyun? \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) wali shakal saaf batati hai ke \(y\) kis raftaar (rate) se badal raha hai. Differential form \(M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\) us waqt kaam aati hai jab humein variables alag karne hon ya integrate karna ho. Dono mein maloomat bilkul ek hi hai, sirf likhne ka andaaz alag hai:
\[M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{M}{N}, \quad N \ne 0\]
Yani \(M\,dx\) ko doosri taraf le jayein aur \(N\,dx\) se divide kar dein, to wapas pehli shakal mil jati hai.
Kitab do misaalein deti hai jin mein dono shaklein saath saath likhi hain:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab ne (i) ko differential form mein badalne ka qadam nahi dikhaya, to hum khud karte hain. Pehle cross multiply (aamne saamne zarb) karein, phir saari terms ek taraf le aayein:
\[(y - x)\,dy = (x + y)\,dx\]
\[(x + y)\,dx - (y - x)\,dy = 0\]
\[(x + y)\,dx + (x - y)\,dy = 0\]
Aakhri line mein sirf yeh kiya ke \(-(y - x) = x - y\), yani minus andar le gaye to dono terms ke sign badal gaye. Isi tarah (ii) mein \(y\,dy = -x\,dx\) hai; \(-x\,dx\) ko left par le jayein to \(x\,dx + y\,dy = 0\) ban jata hai. Yahan \(M = x\) aur \(N = y\) hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{x}\) ko differential form mein likhiye. Is mein \(M\) kya hai aur \(N\) kya?
(Jawab: \(y\,dx - x\,dy = 0\), to \(M = y\) aur \(N = -x\). Sign ka khaas khayal rakhiye.)

Kitab kehti hai: differential equation ka solution ek aisa function hai jo kisi interval \(I\) par defined ho aur equation ko identity bana de. Identity ka matlab hai aisi barabari jo \(I\) ke har \(x\) ke liye sach ho. Yani function aur us ki derivative ko equation mein rakhein to dono sides bilkul ek jaisi ho jayein.

Ab ek khaas qisam ki shart (condition) dekhiye:
\[y = y_0 \ \text{at} \ x = x_0\]
jise mukhtasar tor par yun likhte hain:
\[y(x_0) = y_0\]

Is shart ko initial value condition ya one point boundary condition kehte hain. Aur jab differential equation ke saath aisi ek initial value condition bhi di gayi ho, to is jore ko Initial Value Problem (IVP) kehte hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahi, samjhane ke liye hamari apni hai. Equation lijiye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\). Function \(y = x^2 + c\) is ka solution hai, \(c\) koi bhi constant ho, kyunke \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^2 + c) = 2x\) aur equation identity ban jati hai. Har \(c\) ke liye ek alag curve (parabola) milta hai; yeh poora khandaan (family) general solution kehlata hai.
Ab agar shart di jaye \(y(0) = 3\), yani jab \(x = 0\) ho to \(y = 3\), to: \(3 = 0^2 + c\), is liye \(c = 3\). Ab sirf ek curve bacha: \(y = x^2 + 3\). Yeh particular solution hai.
Misaal ke tor par: ek hi shakal ke bahut se parabola upar neeche rakhe hon; initial condition batati hai ke humein woh wala chahiye jo point \((0, 3)\) se guzarta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aage kya aayega? Is section mein do qisam ki equations solve karenge:
4.2.1 Separable: jahan right side ko (sirf \(x\) ka function) \(\times\) (sirf \(y\) ka function) mein toda ja sake.
4.2.2 Homogeneous: jahan right side sirf ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) par munhasir ho; wahan \(y = vx\) rakh kar equation ko separable bana lete hain.
Is liye har sawal mein pehla kaam ek hi hai: equation ko \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) ki shakal mein likhiye aur phir \(f\) ko ghaur se dekhiye ke woh kis qisam ka hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(y = 5x^2\) equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\) ka solution hai?
(Jawab: nahi. \(\frac{d}{dx}(5x^2) = 10x\), jo \(2x\) ke barabar nahi. Solution banne ke liye equation har \(x\) par identity honi chahiye.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. First order, first degree equation ko hamesha \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) ya \(M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\) likh sakte hain; dono ek hi baat hain.
2. Solution woh function hai jo interval \(I\) par equation ko identity bana de.
3. General solution mein ek arbitrary constant hota hai; yeh curves ka poora khandaan hai.
4. Initial value condition \(y(x_0) = y_0\) us constant ki value fix kar deti hai. Equation + initial condition = Initial Value Problem (IVP).
5. IVP mein pehle general solution nikalein, phir \(x_0\) aur \(y_0\) rakh kar constant maloom karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Differential form banate waqt sign kho dena: \((y - x)\,dy = (x + y)\,dx\) mein jo term doosri taraf jati hai us ka sign badalta hai.
2. \(y(x_0) = y_0\) ko "\(y\) zarb \(x_0\)" samajh lena. Is ka matlab hai: jab \(x = x_0\) ho to \(y\) ki value \(y_0\) hai.
3. Arbitrary constant bhool jana: us ke baghair aap ke paas sirf ek solution hai, general solution nahi, aur IVP solve hi nahi ho sakta.
